statement: Full all-place Selmer sections stay Selmer in finite étale neighbourhoods; compactifications yield adelic points surviving every finite torsor.
depends_on: Harari–Stix Theorem 2.1; definition of Selmer section
notes: No omissions at 2 or at the coefficient prime; real local data are connected components.

statement: Full Selmer plus finite support on a density-one set of finite places implies a point or rational cusp section; the target finite-descent equality consequence holds.
notes: Repairs real-fibre issue in Stoll Proposition8.5; density-one concerns support, not the all-place Selmer input. No additional finiteness assumption on all W(Q) is needed.

statement: For q=a u^e h(u), the cusp-packet map is b↦κ(a)+eb; each Fermat–Legendre cusp has q-class −8κ(2)+2ℓκ(u).
depends_on: Kummer theory; formal Tate j expansion
answers: A.1(iii); correction to R3 and Steklov ramification proposition
notes: All three coordinate cusp divisors included; formal unit uniquely divisible.

statement: The asserted cusp divisibility by ℓ in LM6 E.8 and Steklov's general ramification-divisibility proposition is false.
notes: Counterexample ℓ=5 over Q2: valuation−8≡2; explicit tame matrices generate order20. Reducibility theorem survives after repair.

statement: Corrected local quadratic twists are unramified outside 2ℓ, finite flat/weight2 at ℓ, and tame of conductor exponent1 at2, for every point and cusp case.
notes: Includes ramified splitting twists, good ordinary/supersingular reduction, coefficient prime, and all cusp types.

statement: The mod-ℓ Legendre representation of a Selmer section of Uℓ is reducible and has a quadratic twist with semisimplification 1⊕χℓ; the irreducibility test has level2.
depends_on: A.5; Khare–Wintenberger I Theorem9.1; Kisin hypothesis(H); Serre1972 local inertia statements
notes: Level2 sharpens bound16; genera of all levels dividing16 computed. Serre1972 Propositions11–12 pp273–275 and Kisin author manuscript Theorem(0.1), Corollary(0.2), pp1–2 now opened and read; source-access checks closed.

statement: The cyclic-ℓ Legendre cover maps nonconstantly over Q to Y0(4ℓ); section-supporting components are geometric and g(X0(4ℓ))=(ℓ−3)/2.
depends_on: Explicit two-isogeny construction; modular genus formula
notes: Cyclic4 subgroup is the dual-isogeny inverse image of the second marked2torsion point; includes ℓ=5.

statement: Every full profinite Selmer section of Uℓ/Q is cuspidal for every prime ℓ≥5.
depends_on: A.1–A.2; A.6–A.7; Stoll Corollary8.8; Mazur Theorem(8)
notes: Point case excluded by simultaneous full2torsion and ℓtorsion, using dual ℓisogeny when the invariant line has cyclotomic character.

statement: Y1(7)(Q) is nonempty; y²−xy−4y=x³−4x² has discriminant−1664 and (0,0) of exact order7.
answers: A.1(vii); R5; Steklov Theorem5.14 last sentence
notes: Refuted statement is Y1(7)(Q)=∅; R5's correction is proved.

statement: Every full profinite Selmer section of U3/Q is cuspidal; its compactification is X0(27) and has exactly the three rational cusps.
depends_on: A.2; Stoll Corollary8.8; Kriz–Li §10.1; exact rational transformation and reductions
notes: Exact model v²+v=u³−7; #E(F5)=6 and #E(F7)=9. A.14 also supplies exact L nonvanishing and finiteSha independently.

statement: Every full profinite Selmer section of the plus Fermat curve Un/Q is cuspidal for all odd n≥3, with exactly three rational cusp centres.
depends_on: A.8; A.10; finite étale power maps
answers: A.1(ix); odd Selmer part of R7
notes: Does not use the local section theorem or any global density assertion.

statement: The three classical quartic quotients are E−:y²=x³−4x and twice E+:y²=x³+4x; all have geometric CM ring Z[i], and Jac(C4) is Q-isogenous to E−×E+².
depends_on: Explicit birational maps; Klein-four differential decomposition
answers: A.3 quartic case; A.4 CM and Jacobian; moonshine M4(b)
notes: Z[sqrt(−2)] assertion for these quotients is false; rational endomorphism ring is Z.

statement: Exact Mordell–Weil groups are E−(Q)=C2×C2 and E+(Q)=C4, with complete explicit point lists.
depends_on: Explicit2isogeny descent; primitive quartic obstructions mod16; good reduction at3,5
notes: No numerical rank table used; each quotient's rational points on v²=1±u⁴ are listed.

statement: Exact eta-product positivity proves L(E27,1), L(E−,1), L(E+,1)>0, and Rubin gives finite Tate–Shafarevich groups.
depends_on: Martin–Ono Theorem2; Mellin integral; Rubin1987 TheoremA and Remark(3), pp527–528
answers: A.4 finiteSha; A.3; supplemental R6 arithmetic
notes: All factors positive on imaginary axis; no floating-point or denominator estimate needed. Primary Rubin pages visually inspected.

statement: Each of the three elliptic quotients separately proves every full profinite Selmer section of classical C4/Q is one of its four rational cusp packets.
answers: A.3 quartic; A.4 three separate quotient proofs
notes: Full all-place Selmer hypothesis retained; no local section conjecture used.

statement: For every n≥3, full profinite Selmer sections of classical Cn/Q are precisely images of its rational cusp packets, three centres for odd n and four for even n.
depends_on: A.11; A.15; finite étale power maps
notes: All-section version requires the separate all-place local point-or-cusp statement. Real packet parametrization deferred to root local analysis.
